The production adapter is `apps/api/story_game_routes.py`,
`apps/api/story_game_runtime.py` and the consolidated reset baseline
`supabase/migrations/202610180001_initial_schema.sql`. Formal composition and
consent already live in `202610180001_initial_schema.sql`. Applying a migration
and deploying these sources are separate from passing disposable tests.

## Authority and source evidence

Every job binds the owned project, policy epoch, source inventory, preferences,
execution generation, current delivered Shape reply, immutable formal edition,
manuscript digest and separate consent revision. `story_game_context` takes the
same project/profile/lifetime locks as formal composition and verifies current
full completion plus exact-edition consent. No client-supplied source list,
completion flag, person ID or candidate JSON is authority.

The provider sees only the claimed edition's original-backed chapter blocks.
`stage_story_game` resolves the stored chapter and block, requires each quote to
be an exact, unambiguous substring, and derives original source/version/offsets
from the verified formal chapter. Factual scene titles and person labels must
also occur in that quote. Extra fields, unsupported quotes, duplicate person
labels, HTML and unsupported art keys are rejected. The model cannot approve its
own output. A completed provider response is a proposal, never a publication.

The initial runtime supports exactly two scenes and two represented people.
Private server-side person records bind the exact passage to an opaque adaptation
person ID; they do not claim to be a resolved genealogical family tree. The author
must confirm that the two source descriptions identify distinct adults and grant
permission for their exact passages before publication. Unknown ages, minors or
uncertain identity cannot be approved through this version. Aliasing does not
anonymize names or relationships inside a source quote; the review shows both.

`begin_story_game` serializes the project and reuses an existing current job.
Each request UUID replays only its original authority. A new request can replace
stale work after fresh completion and consent. States are `pending`, `running`,
`review_required`, `published`, `failed`, `stale`. Claims use a fresh fencing token,
a 180-second lease and at most three attempts; a busy lease cannot dispatch twice.
Read, stage, publish and delivery all recheck current authority. A late worker
cannot stage after a replacement claim or consent/source change.

The host constructs all browser IDs, generic aliases, allowlisted scenery and
bounded coordinates. The review includes every scene title, alias, quotation,
protagonist and scenery choice. Publication requires the exact database candidate
digest and two separate person permission confirmations. The database derives the
authenticated reviewer and records the candidate, permissions, purpose and private
audience atomically. Replaying the same approved candidate returns stored state.
The browser cannot replace reviewed content at publication.

`request.schema.json` / `candidate.schema.json` fixtures use their own sorted,
compact JSON conventions. The fixture validator remains a design/development aid,
not the runtime authorization service. `game.schema.json` describes the actual
browser projection.

All routes below use the existing authenticated project owner and `no-store`.

| Route under `/v1/agent/projects/{project_id}` | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /story-game` | Read completion, consent and adaptation metadata. |
| `POST /formal-memoir` | Explicitly begin a complete extractive formal edition. |
| `POST /formal-memoir/advance` | Advance the owner's current run by at most eight chapters. |
| `PUT /story-game/consent` | Grant/revoke separate consent for the exact edition and digest. |
| `POST /story-game` | Begin/replay a job and perform one bounded proposal attempt. |

# Two-step game runtime

The skill has two model operations:

1. Composer chapters plus the canonical timeline produce a source-linked scene plan.
2. Astra turns the validated scenes into an HTML/CSS webpage. The host validates the page and injects its trusted movement, interaction and text-version runtime.

`apps/api/story_game_runtime.py` implements both operations. Each receives the shared skill instructions and its phase prompt (`proposal.md` or `webpage.md`). Model responses follow `schemas/scenes.schema.json` and `schemas/webpage.schema.json`. The page builder uses `MEMORY_SPARK_STORY_GAME_BUILD_MODEL`, defaulting to the verified `gpt-6-astra` binding; scene planning uses the composer model setting.

## Input and completion

The authenticated host reads the current composer snapshot and its canonical event dependencies. The `chapters` input contains the composer's saved prose sections, titles and source references; `timeline` contains the corresponding canonical event records, including supported stages, dates and uncertainty. Composer prose replaces the old extractive-only game input. One to 128 scenes cover the supplied timeline. A person can recur, and a memory marker can have `person=null`.

Validation requires exact chapter quotations, matching title/person substrings, valid chapter/event references and complete event coverage. The webpage must contain the required control slots, permitted static HTML/CSS and supplied UI text. Model-written scripts, event handlers, external resources, frames, forms and additional personal claims are rejected. Successful completion returns the scenes and validated webpage. A build failure leaves the job retryable; a partial plan is not delivered as a game.

## Host integration

The existing authenticated game action owns admission and persistence. It keeps the current Shape/source/policy checks, formal source-completion fence and edition-bound adaptation consent outside the skill. The UI's create action prepares those host records when needed. It requires a completed, current composer snapshot; it does not ask the user to build a second memoir manually.

A job binds the composer snapshot/digest/revision, source/event/policy/preferences, current Shape reply, formal edition and consent revision. Claims have a 360-second lease and three attempts. Each model-body send, final save and delivery rechecks the host authority. The two-call generation deadline is 330 seconds. Source or consent changes withhold stale results.

After a successful build, the host stores the private game and returns `published`. There is no game-review screen, per-person approval form or publish action in the creation flow. No human approval receipt is manufactured. The browser opens the saved game immediately and can reopen it without another model call.

## Playback

The generated document runs in a frame with `sandbox="allow-scripts"` and an opaque origin. The host adds a nonce-protected script and a restrictive content-security policy. Astra supplies static markup and styles; only the trusted host script runs. The page has no network access, parent-page access or storage privileges. Keyboard/touch movement, connected scenes, memoir interactions and a complete text version use the existing runtime. Escape, closure, project/phase changes and revocation remove the frame.

Saving, access control and display belong to the host UI. Public hosting, external recipients and public links are not authorized by private workspace generation.

The older request/candidate fixture validator is a development artifact, not the two-step runtime's admission service or model contract.

# Scene selection and separate game builder

Memoir owns two planning calls on `MEMORY_SPARK_MEMOIR_COMPOSER_MODEL`:

1. Chapters plus the canonical timeline produce a full scene pool, with recommendations.
2. After the owner confirms scene IDs, the selected subset produces the final creative brief.

`apps/api/story_game_runtime.py` runs these calls using the shared skill and
`proposal.md` or `brief.md`. The independently installed `higgsfield-websites`
skill then runs on Astra through `apps/api/higgsfield_game.py`. Its content stays
outside Memoir's prompt sources and Langfuse catalog. See
[the host setup guide](../../../docs/story-game-scene-selection.md) for updates.

## Pool and human confirmation

The host reads completed composer prose and the full canonical timeline under
current Shape, formal-edition, adaptation-consent and source/policy fences.
One to 128 distinct options must cover every supplied event. Each has an exact,
unambiguous chapter quotation, an exact title/person substring, supported event
IDs, a recommendation flag and a short reason. Life stages come from those events;
an option cannot combine stages. Every represented stage needs a recommendation.
Input over the bounded capacity fails explicitly rather than silently dropping events.

The durable job moves from `pending` through `running` to `selection_required`.
It has no worker lease while waiting for the owner and no build is dispatched.
The owner receives options grouped by life stage, editable count and checkboxes,
and a notice that more scenes increase generation cost and time. Recommendations
are initial checkbox values, never approval. Confirmation sends the exact pool
digest and option IDs. PostgreSQL verifies ownership, current source authority,
unique nonempty IDs and the digest, then saves the confirmation. It orders choices
by the original pool and records the owner, time and selection digest. Repeating
the same selection is idempotent; changing a confirmed set is rejected. A selected
subset need not cover every event: full coverage applies to the pool.

## Brief and delegated build

The build claim requires that saved confirmation. The composer sees only selected
scene text and returns a creative brief plus their complete ordered indices.
The host validates and saves it; retries reuse the saved brief. The final request
contains the brief, selected scenes, locale, UI labels and Memoir export contract.
Unselected passages and private chapter/event/source identities do not reach Astra.

The private worker loads a snapshot of the separate skill's Markdown files. Astra
can read its game references and validate the webpage through bounded tools.
It must read the entrypoint, game flow, design system and stylization reference,
and validate the complete HTML. The final model output references the saved
artifact digest, avoiding a second copy of the entire document. Only this tool
loop uses `gpt-6-astra`; planning calls use the composer setting. A receipt records
all response IDs, the managed prompt manifest and the installed skill digest.

This adapter targets the existing offline Memoir player: the generated artifact
contains static HTML/CSS and generic scenery; Memoir supplies movement, NPC memory
interactions, connected scenes and the complete text version. Upstream Cloudflare
scaffolding, generated media, shell commands, account requirements and public
Higgsfield deployment do not apply to this export target. The original upstream
skill remains unmodified and can still be used separately with its normal CLI.

## Authority, retries and playback

Pool claims last 180 seconds with a 150-second deadline. Brief plus game building
has a 900-second lease and 840-second deadline, including a bounded 780-second,
12-round Astra loop. Each phase allows three explicit attempts. Every provider
body send, final save and protected delivery rechecks source, consent, composer
snapshot and job authority. No authority locks are held while a provider generates.
Revocation withholds old content and clears saved planning projections.

The final save must exactly match the confirmed scene subset and its digest.
Success saves the game for immediate private play and links the project URL;
there is no extra person-permission or publishing approval screen. Existing host
sharing controls can later grant public or invited-friend access.

The document runs in an opaque-origin `sandbox="allow-scripts"` frame. A nonce
permits only Memoir's trusted movement script. Validation rejects model scripts,
handlers, extra biographical text, external assets, links, frames and CSS URLs.
The frame has no network, parent-page access or storage privileges. Closing,
navigation, project/phase changes and source revocation remove it.

# Scene selection and resumable NovelToGame builds

The default builder is NovelToGame with GPT-6.1 Sol max. Planning uses the same
model and effort. `MEMOIR_GAME_BUILDER=higgsfield` selects the independently
installed Astra backup; failure never silently starts a second provider.

## Selection and authority

`story_game_runtime.py` proposes a grounded pool covering the complete approved
composer/timeline snapshot. The UI groups options by source life stage and checks
recommendations by default. Owners can change the count and individual options.
More scenes increase time and cost. Recommendations are not confirmation.
The exact saved pool digest and nonempty scene IDs must be confirmed by the owner
before the build claim. The original pool order determines the selected sequence.
A selected subset need not cover the complete timeline. PostgreSQL validates the
source quotations, selected IDs, consent, edition and current source authority.

The confirmed subset produces a saved creative brief. Retries reuse that brief.
Only selected quotations and their timeline metadata enter the builder; other
passages and private source references remain outside the build requests/player.
Repeated options from one chapter become separate supported memory stops.

## NovelToGame stages

The private worker runs `apps/api/novel_game.py`: analyze, concept, design,
whitebox, art and production. Each loads its unmodified upstream skill/references
from the reviewed `deps/novel-to-game` revision, plus Memoir's managed adapter,
journey policy and stage prompt. Art/build also consume the asset policy.
The host verifies upstream bytes against `deps/novel-to-game.lock.json` without
requiring Git inside deployed containers. Dependency upgrades refresh this lock.

Successful stage outputs and real model receipts are stored in a service-only
PostgreSQL checkpoint table, keyed by game, stage and exact request hash.
A retry with unchanged input reuses them. Every checkpoint read/write and provider
body send rechecks the job/source/consent fence. No generation holds an authority
lock while waiting for a model. Partial/failed builds never become playable.

Design returns a validated continuous `JOURNEY_PLAN.json`. The fixed runtime
allows both-direction keyboard/touch walking, smooth reversible scene transitions,
unlimited proximity reading before/after completion, unique-memory progress,
source text, reduced motion, ending and restart. Models supply data and styling;
they cannot supply executable HTML/JavaScript. The application art pass binds
source-supported locations to the original shared illustrated place library.
The standalone adapter can additionally prepare new scene illustrations through
its explicit image-generation workflow. Shared avatars, UI and music are reused.
A missing age uses an explicitly unspecified stage and imagined generic avatar.

The host plays the whitebox before art, then runs complete desktop and touch
production replays. Final receipts require six upstream checks: launch, render,
input, coreLoop, outcome and restart. These observations establish technical
playability, not subjective fun or physical-device coverage.

## Saving and playback

Pool claims last 300 seconds with a 280-second deadline. Build claims last
3600 seconds with a 3480-second deadline; individual model stages are bounded.
The final save requires the original selection digest and verified model/build
receipt, and checks every displayed passage against that selection.
The game is immediately available privately through Memoir's existing project
URL. Public and invited-friend sharing remain host controls, without another
publication approval screen in this skill.

The NovelToGame artifact is validated journey/source/CSS data. The browser loads
the host-owned runtime and public generic artwork, then creates an opaque-origin
`sandbox="allow-scripts"` frame. Only the trusted runtime receives a script nonce.
The frame permits image/audio requests solely to the application's hashed stock
asset path; it cannot connect, submit forms, navigate the parent, or use storage.
Closing, project/phase changes and source revocation remove the frame.
The legacy Higgsfield adapter retains its strict static-markup validator and
trusted player. Its upstream instructions remain separate and updatable.

All Memoir model-consumed prompts live in the managed Langfuse catalog. Review
and merge Markdown to main before publishing actual numeric versions and receipts.

name: memoir/skills/story-game/webpage
content:
Build a polished, responsive side-scrolling webpage game from the supplied scenes.
Produce a complete HTML5 document containing inline CSS, validated and returned
through the host's artifact tool. Use the supplied locale and UI strings. Give the journey a coherent visual
identity, with distinct scenery for the scenes and clear keyboard/touch controls.

Memoir injects its trusted movement and interaction runtime after validation.
Produce the page's markup and styling; the runtime fills titles, character labels,
memory passages and the text version from the supplied scenes. Use these elements
exactly once inside a root with id `memoir-game`:

- `.game-framing`: an empty paragraph for the perspective notice.
- `.game-stage`: a focusable region (`tabindex="0"`) containing `.game-world`,
  which contains `.game-player`. The stage clips its horizontally moving world.
- `.game-scene-label`: an empty heading or paragraph with `aria-live="polite"`.
- `.game-controls`: a group containing buttons with `data-game-move="-1"`,
  `data-game-interact`, and `data-game-move="1"`.
- `.game-dialogue`: an initially hidden element with `role="status".
- `details.game-text-equivalent`: a details element containing a summary.

The world uses pixel coordinates and a width of 1280 pixels. The runtime positions
the player and character buttons, clamps movement, connects adjacent scenes and
handles camera movement. Style `.game-npc` buttons for character silhouettes or
memory markers. Keep the player and NPCs positioned absolutely within the world.
The stage gets `data-scene-index="0"`, `"1"`, etc.; use those selectors for distinct
backgrounds. Keep scenery generic and source-consistent, without reconstructing
private addresses or recognizable likenesses. Use CSS shapes and inline SVG.

Include visible focus states, 44-pixel touch targets, readable contrast, responsive
layout and a `prefers-reduced-motion` rule. Use supplied UI strings for visible text;
leave personal narrative slots empty for the runtime. No additional biographical
text is needed. The complete text version must remain available.

The document runs offline in an isolated frame. Use inline CSS and system fonts.
Allowed elements are html, head, meta (charset/viewport only), title, body, main,
header, footer, section, div, p, span, h1–h4, button, details, summary, style, svg,
g, path, rect, circle, ellipse, line, polyline and polygon. Omit scripts, event
handler attributes, links, forms, frames, remote assets, CSS URLs and imports.
The host supplies all JavaScript. Do not add consent, review, publish or approval
controls. Follow the handoff adapter's artifact return format.
